GMO Payment Service, Inc., a consolidated subsidiary, acts as the payment provider: it screens consumers' creditworthiness, pays the sales amount on behalf of the shop, and later collects the sales amount from the consumer and bills them. From shops, it receives a fixed monthly fee (stock) and fees according to the use of the service (fee and spread). The securities report also lists Atokara, a BNPL service that also supports installment and in-person transactions with Sumitomo Mitsui Card Company, Limited, alongside it as a deferred payment service.
entries.440daf441f00c170: Its sales are mainly to merchants. The report’s management analysis states that in online billing and recurring billing for the fiscal year ended September 2025, online payments for travel, tickets, food and beverages increased due to the going live of new merchants and expanded payments by existing merchants. In the in-person field, the report says cashless payment use advanced among merchants in industries and business types that people use daily. In the Finance-Related Business’s “GMO Atobarai,” the company, acting as a payment provider, assesses consumers’ creditworthiness and, on behalf of merchants, bills and collects payment from consumers. The borrowers for overseas lending are overseas FinTech operators, and the report states that the development of new borrowers and additional lending progressed, centered on North America and India. No single external customer accounted for 10% or more of revenue in the fiscal year ended September 2025. The previous fiscal year, ended September 2024, Sumitomo Mitsui Card Company, Limited accounted for 10% or more of consolidated revenue, and the report omits its disclosure because revenue from that company in the fiscal year ended September 2025 was below 10%. In the table dividing revenue from external customers by region, Japan accounts for the majority.

entries.55b143dcb672e79b: This business links payment information between shops such as online retailers (called 'merchants' in the securities report) and payment providers such as credit card companies. It is divided into two types depending on the contract method: direct merchant contracts, under which shops contract individually with each payment provider, and representative merchant contracts, under which the company's group concludes contracts with payment providers collectively and also handles the collection of sales proceeds in a lump sum. Fees received from shops are divided into initial fees (initial), fixed monthly fees (stock) and per-transaction fees (fee); representative merchant contracts also add a fee on sales proceeds (spread). Its main services are payment processing for online billing and recurring billing, and in-person payment processing, and it also works on BaaS (Banking as a Service) support for financial institutions and businesses. For banks, it offers Bank Pay, developed jointly with The Bank of Yokohama, Ltd., and the GMO-PG Processing Platform, which bundles the services needed to start a new payment business. Revenue including inter-segment transactions for the fiscal year ended September 2025 was ¥61.677405 billion (up 10.3% year on year), and segment profit (operating profit) was ¥29.779631 billion (up 18.1% year on year), making it the largest of the 3 reportable segments. The company also cites growth in revenue from its processing platform services. In January 2025, Enpei Inc. (now GMO Enpei, Inc.), which promotes cashless payments and DX in the childcare and education industries, became a subsidiary of the company.

entries.7ec2c1a6cf79ee35: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended September 2025 was ¥31,340,267 thousand (up 24.4% year on year), and the report states that the company achieved its earnings forecast for the current consolidated fiscal year. Segment profit (operating profit) was ¥29,779,631 thousand (up 18.1%) for the Payment Agency Business, ¥5,407,577 thousand (up 31.7%) for the Finance-Related Business, and ¥418,053 thousand (up 11.9%) for the Payment Activation Business. Consolidated operating profit is the total of the three segments less adjustments such as corporate expenses not allocated to reportable segments. The reasons the report cites are: in the Payment Agency Business, although one-time costs were incurred, the share of online payments and in-person recurring revenue, which have higher gross profit margins than initial-fee revenue, increased; and in the Finance-Related Business, improved credit accuracy in deferred payment kept the uncollected rate low and stable, and remittance services and lending to overseas FinTech operators grew. Profit before tax was ¥31,911,317 thousand (up 16.0%). The report states that the increase was smaller than that of operating profit mainly because a gain of ¥1,629,664 thousand on the sale of an equity-method investment was recorded in the previous fiscal year. Profit attributable to owners of the parent increased 16.7%.

entries.8d5171b7afda7a79: GMO Payment Gateway, Inc. earns revenue mainly through payment agency services that connect shops such as online retailers (called “merchants” in the report) with credit card companies and other payment providers, combined with financial services such as deferred payment, lending and remittance and support services that help shops increase sales. The [[term:annual-securities-report|Annual Securities Report]] (hereinafter, “the report”) divides its business into three [[term:segment|reportable segments]]: Payment Agency Business, Finance-Related Business and Payment Activation Business. Revenue for the fiscal year ended September 2025 was ¥82,499,385 thousand (up 11.8% year on year), and the audit report in the report states that revenue from the Payment Agency Business accounts for 74.8% of consolidated revenue and the Finance-Related Business for 23.3%. Revenue from the Payment Agency Business is disclosed in four items: initial fees, monthly fixed fees (stock), per-transaction fees (fee), and spread fees (commissions on sales proceeds under representative merchant contracts).
entries.8e6b91c9ddac2fe7: The core is the payment agency service, which connects payment information between businesses selling online (merchants) and payment providers such as credit card companies. Merchants can efficiently use payment methods such as credit card payments, convenience store payment collection, electronic money, QR code payments and direct debit. In online billing and recurring billing, the company and GMO Epsilon Inc. are responsible; in the in-person field, GMO Financial Gate, Inc. is responsible; and overseas payment agency is handled by GMO-Z.COM PAYMENT GATEWAY PTE. LTD. and others. There is also BaaS (Banking as a Service) support for financial institutions and businesses, including “Ginkō Pay,” co-developed with The Bank of Yokohama, Ltd., and the “GMO-PG Processing Platform,” which provides a range of services for launching a new payment business. Added to these are the Finance-Related Business, which offers early payment, transaction lending to merchants, lending to overseas FinTech operators, remittance, “Sokkyū byGMO,” “Seikyūsho Kādo-barai byGMO,” and deferred payment (“GMO Atobarai,” “GMO Kakebarai,” and “Atokara,” developed jointly with Sumitomo Mitsui Card Company, Limited), and the Payment Activation Business, which offers marketing support, security enhancement and the medical-specialized reservation management system “Medical Kakumei byGMO.”

entries.92d3c616fc6773e1: A business of money-related services such as deferred payment, remittance, financing for stores and early payment (the filing calls it the Money Service Business: MSB). It provides an early payment service that helps improve merchants' cash flow, transaction lending, which is financing for merchants, lending to overseas FinTech operators, a remittance service, "Sokkyu byGMO," an instant salary receipt service, and "Invoice Card Payment byGMO," which enables card payment of invoices in business-to-business (BtoB) transactions. Through the consolidated subsidiary GMO Payment Service, Inc., it also handles deferred payment such as "GMO Atobarai," "GMO Kakebarai" and "Atokara." Revenue including inter-segment transactions for the fiscal year ended September 2025 was ¥19,188,123 thousand (up 16.6% year on year), and segment profit (operating profit) was ¥5,407,577 thousand (up 31.7% year on year); it is the second-largest business after the payment processing business. The company cites the contribution of BNPL services and "GMO Kakebarai" while growth in the EC market for goods remained low, growth in lending to overseas FinTech operators driven by new borrowers and additional loans mainly in North America and India, and improved credit screening accuracy in deferred payment that kept the uncollected rate stable at a low level.

entries.e7ff7b3d501952d2: It handles payments in person, such as at shop counters. GMO Financial Gate, Inc., a consolidated subsidiary, provides in-person payment processing services for credit card payments, debit card payments, barcode payments, QR code payments and others. Under direct merchant contracts, the company also receives the cost of payment terminals from merchants. For the fiscal year ended September 2025, initial revenue from terminal sales decreased, mainly due to the reversal of a large project booked in the prior year and stronger marketing of terminal-free payment solutions for small and medium-sized enterprises. On the other hand, cashless payments spread among merchants in industries and business formats used in daily life, and the company explains that recurring revenue exceeded its plan.
entries.e9226942c50eef83: A deferred payment service for business-to-business (BtoB) transactions. It is provided by GMO Payment Service, Inc. For the fiscal year ended September 2025, the company explains that this “GMO Kakebarai”, together with the BNPL service, contributed to the growth in revenue of the deferred payment services.
entries.e956cc260a269888: In the Payment Agency Business, as service usage fees, it receives from merchants initial fees, monthly fixed fees (stock), and usage-based fees according to the number of transactions processed (fee), and in the in-person field it also receives the price of payment terminals. Under “representative merchant contracts,” in which the company group concludes contracts with payment providers collectively and also handles the receipt of sales proceeds in one batch, the company group additionally earns a commission on sales proceeds (spread). Revenue for the fiscal year ended September 2025 was ¥82,499,385 thousand (up 11.8% year on year). Year-on-year changes by item were: initial fees down 23.4%, stock up 19.9%, fee up 16.4%, and spread up 20.4%. The report states that initial fees declined as a reflection of a reversal of large in-person projects booked in the previous fiscal year, while stock, fee and spread progressed steadily. The number of payments processed was up 17.4% year on year, and the amount processed was up 16.5% (total for online billing, recurring billing, in-person and “GMO Atobarai”). The report’s accounting policies state that revenue is recognized at the time of delivery for sales of payment terminals and other equipment; monthly for usage-based fees of payment agency services; and evenly over the contract period for fixed fees. The report also states that for transactions in which it acts as an intermediary or agent, it decides individually whether to present revenue on a gross or net basis, and that either presentation does not affect net profit or loss. Revenue of the Finance-Related Business includes interest income under the effective interest method of IFRS 9, which Note 27 classifies as “revenue recognized from other sources,” and this interest income accounts for a majority of the Finance-Related Business’s revenue.

entries.f9146f390994d99a: It connects payment information between online shops and credit card companies and other payment providers. The company and GMO Epsilon, Inc. provide a payment processing service that efficiently delivers credit card payments, convenience store payments, e-money, QR code payments, Pay-easy, cash on delivery, direct debit, PayPal, carrier billing, online bank payments, multi-currency payments and more. Payment processing services in other countries are provided by GMO-Z.COM PAYMENT GATEWAY PTE. LTD. and others. For the fiscal year ended September 2025, the company explains that revenue rose as new merchants went live and existing merchants expanded their payments, increasing online payments for travel and tickets and for food and beverages. Online payment revenue of the company on a standalone basis rose 19.1%.
